description:
FILED s468be (Opus), found while attributing the companion ROW DIFF; the
minimal reproducer below was probed against perl 5.40.3.  PRE-EXISTING.

REPRODUCER (three files, no module, no encoding pragma anywhere):

    # tiny.pl -- the ONLY non-ASCII byte is U+2019 inside a COMMENT
    # a comment with a curly quote â in it
    $main::v = 42;
    1;

    # q.pl
    do "./tiny.pl" or die $@||$!;
    print "v=$main::v\n";

    perl q.pl     ->  v=42
    ./runpcl q.pl ->  PCL: cannot parse (inline code): PPI failed to tokenize
                      it at (eval 1) line 1.

THE ASYMMETRY IS THE FINDING.  The very same tiny.pl:
  * `./pl2cl < tiny.pl`  transpiles it fine;
  * `./runpcl tiny.pl`   runs it fine (a print variant prints "ok").
So the file-mode source path copes with the byte and the run-time `do FILE`
path does not â `do FILE` reaches PCL's INLINE-CODE parse (the "(eval 1)"
in the message is that path's marker), and that parse is where the byte kills
the tokenizer.  Whatever the file-mode path does to the source before PPI sees
it (decode / layer / repair), the inline path does not.

WHAT IT COSTS TODAY.  t/op/closure.t:721 is

    do "./op/closure_test.pl" or die $@||$!;
    is $closure_test::s2->()(), '10 cubes',
      'cloning closure proto with no CvOUTSIDE';

and t/op/closure_test.pl's header comment contains "this fileâs main CV" â
one U+2019.  That single character is the file's whole remaining abort and its
whole remaining shortfall (I2 row `t/op/closure.t 6 -> 1` after #1032).  Proof:
replacing the â with an ASCII apostrophe in a copy makes PCL print "10 cubes",
i.e. the row passes.  Reported by the companion as
`aborted-forms:1: PCL: cannot parse (inline code): PPI failed to tokenize it`.

WHERE TO LOOK.  The `do FILE` runtime implementation and PCL's inline-code
parse entry (the same one string eval uses).  Ask FIRST whether the two paths
read the file with different layers/decoding â this smells like the file-mode
path binmode-ing or byte-reading the source while the inline path hands PPI a
string that has been through a decode (or has not been, where PPI needs it).
Guard when fixed: a Pl/t row with a non-ASCII byte in a COMMENT of a `do`-ne
file, plus the same file `require`d and string-eval'd (the three spellings
should agree).

=== DONE (s470bi) ===
TWO INDEPENDENT SILENT DEFECTS, both hit by ONE U+2019 in a COMMENT.

  1. `p-do` sized its buffer with FILE-LENGTH -- OCTETS -- but filled it with
     the DECODED characters and DISCARDED `read-sequence`'s count, so every
     multi-byte character left junk past the end of the text.  PPI then failed
     to tokenize the trailing rubbish and the whole `do` died with
     "PCL: cannot parse (inline code)", where `require` on the same file and
     `pl2cl` on the same file are both fine.
  2. The read used the DEFAULT external format, which decodes UTF-8, where
     perl reads source as OCTETS and lets `use utf8` decide.  A do-ne file
     measured length("â") as 1 where perl -- and PCL's own `require`, which
     transpiles the FILE -- answer 3.

New `cl/pcl-runtime.lisp::%p-read-source-octets` (`:external-format :latin-1`,
honouring the count) is the one reading `do` and any future inline-source entry
share.

THE COMPILER HALF, and it is the decision that needs the octets:
`Pl::Parser::_maybe_decode_utf8` guarded on `!utf8::is_utf8($src)` -- a
question about perl's INTERNAL REPRESENTATION, not about the text.  Source that
reaches the compiler over the `pl2cl --server` pipe (`:encoding(utf-8)` both
sides -- the transport `do FILE` and string eval both use) arrives FLAGGED
while still holding one character per source OCTET, so a `use utf8` file read
as octets was never decoded at all.  The guard is now
`utf8::downgrade($copy, 1)` -- "is every character a byte value?" -- which
yields the octet string when it is and leaves a genuinely decoded source (any
character above 255) alone, exactly as before.  The perl primitives were probed
first (scratch/s469bi/p1084/u.pl).

MEASURED vs perl 5.40.3: `do FILE`, `require FILE` and a string eval of the
same text now agree with perl and with each other -- len 3 for a plain file
(byte semantics), len 1 for a `use utf8` file.  Before: the two `do` shapes
were hard aborts and the `use utf8` shape stayed 3.

GUARD: `Pl/t/utf8-source-01.t` 36 -> 38 rows (the three spellings on one
program, and the `use utf8` variant), inverse-verified against main -- both new
rows fail there with the "cannot parse" abort.  Two files are used, not one,
because perl's `do FILE` populates %INC and a `require` of the SAME path would
then be a no-op -- a divergence of its own, filed as #1116, not baked in here.

RESIDUES FILED: #1115 (PCL's `open` decodes UTF-8 by default where perl reads
BYTES -- srclen 101 vs 107, a general silent-wrong for every slurp of a
non-ASCII file) and #1116 (`do FILE` does not populate %INC).

PAY-OFF: t/op/closure.t:721 `do "./op/closure_test.pl"` was the file's whole
remaining abort (#1083's note); Fable's sweep/companion legs measure it.
subject: `do FILE` re-parses the file through the INLINE-CODE path, which dies on a non-ASCII byte the file-mode path handles â one comment character costs t/op/closure.t its last row
